subject: art-design
topicDisplay: Fine Art Drawing Painting Printmaking Sculpture
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In screen printing, areas you do not want printed are blocked using a...
questions.explain: A stencil on the mesh blocks the ink so it only passes through the open, unblocked areas.

questions.q: Corrugated card is useful in 3D work because it is...
options: Lightweight, strong and easy to score and fold
questions.explain: Corrugated card is light yet rigid, and can be scored and folded to build 3D forms.

questions.q: 'Welding' is a construction method used mainly with...
questions.explain: Welding fuses pieces of metal together using heat, a common method in metal sculpture.

questions.q: Which paint is water-based and dries quickly to a permanent finish?
questions.explain: Acrylic paint is water-based, dries fast and becomes water-resistant once dry.

questions.q: A 'glaze' on ceramics provides...
options: A glassy, often waterproof and decorative coating
questions.explain: A glaze melts in the kiln to form a glassy surface that seals and decorates the pot.

questions.q: A sculpture designed to be viewed from all sides 'in the round' is...
options: A relief carved into a flat background
questions.explain: Sculpture in the round is freestanding and can be walked around and viewed from every angle.

questions.q: The sculpture technique of removing material from a solid block is called...
questions.explain: Carving is a subtractive method, cutting away material from a block of stone or wood.

questions.q: Which method would a sculptor use to make a hollow form from sheet material?
options: Construction by folding and joining sheets
questions.explain: Folding and joining sheet material is a construction method that can create hollow 3D forms.

questions.q: Andy Goldsworthy is known for sculpture made from...
options: Natural materials such as leaves, stone and ice in the landscape
questions.explain: Andy Goldsworthy creates ephemeral land art using natural found materials in the environment.

questions.q: Which medium is a soft, powdery stick available in soft (chalk) or oil form?
questions.explain: Pastels are sticks of pigment, made as soft chalk pastels or richer oil pastels.

questions.q: Collage is an artwork made by...
options: Sticking different materials onto a surface
questions.explain: Collage assembles and glues various materials, such as paper or fabric, onto a surface.

questions.q: What is 'impasto' in painting?
options: Paint thinned to a watery wash
Thick paint applied so brush or knife marks stand out
Painting only in black and white
questions.explain: Impasto is thickly applied paint that leaves visible, textured marks on the surface.

questions.q: Screen printing pushes ink through what?
questions.explain: Screen printing forces ink through a fine mesh, with a stencil blocking areas that stay unprinted.

questions.q: 'Mixed media' work is made by...
options: Combining two or more different materials or media
Printing the same image many times
questions.explain: Mixed media combines different materials, such as paint, ink and collage, in one piece.

questions.q: Which material is most suitable for bending into a flowing linear 3D form?
questions.explain: Wire is easily bent and twisted, making it ideal for linear, gestural 3D forms.

questions.q: What does 'firing' clay in a kiln do?
questions.explain: Firing heats clay to high temperatures, turning it permanently hard and durable.

questions.q: Oil paint is mixed and thinned using...
options: Solvents such as turpentine or linseed oil
questions.explain: Oil paint is oil-based and is thinned and cleaned with solvents like turpentine, not water.

questions.q: Lino printing is an example of which type of printmaking?
questions.explain: In relief printing such as lino, ink sits on the raised surface while cut-away areas stay blank.

questions.q: Etching is a printmaking process that uses what to cut into a metal plate?
questions.explain: In etching, acid bites into exposed lines of a metal plate, which then hold ink for printing.

questions.q: In 3D design, 'structure' refers to...
options: How a form is built and held together to stay stable
questions.explain: Structure concerns how a 3D object is constructed and supported so it stands and holds together.

questions.q: Plaster is most commonly used in 3D work for...
options: Casting solid forms in a mould
questions.explain: Plaster is poured into moulds where it sets, making it a common casting material.

questions.q: What is a 'maquette'?
options: A small preliminary model of a sculpture
questions.explain: A maquette is a small-scale model made to plan and test ideas for a larger sculpture.
